prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts an outdoor scene where the camera wearer starts on a tiled sidewalk next to a stone retaining wall on the left (roughly 0.5–1.5 m away, within arm's reach) and a planted verge with thin multi-stemmed trees on the right (1–3 m away), before turning right across frames 3 to 5 to face a wet asphalt street (spanning roughly 2–10 m ahead) and a building across the road (10–15 m away). A dark rounded cap or helmet rim worn by the camera wearer is partially visible at the bottom edge (~0.1–0.2 m away), and two pedestrians stand together on the sidewalk in frame 3 roughly 12–15 m ahead and 0.5 m from each other, facing away or slightly sideways without looking toward the camera wearer. As the wearer turns right from the sidewalk toward the street, the left stone wall exits the frame, while a thin multi-stemmed tree on the right curb comes within arm's reach (~0.8–1.2 m) in frames 3 and 5 and partially occludes the street behind it. The depth map clearly separates the vertical stone wall, foreground tree branches, and smooth ground plane gradient better than the cluttered RGB textures alone. However, it is unreliable on the camera wearer's foreground cap rim (which flips from medium grey in frames 1–3 to saturated bright white in frames 4–5) and loses the distant pedestrians in frame 3 as well as the building facade across the street in frames 4–5 into uniform black background.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is almost entirely black and fails to segment the scene layout—omitting the sidewalk, left stone wall (0.5–1.5 m away), right-side curb trees (0.8–3 m away), wet road (2–10 m away), and distant building across the street (10–15 m away). In frame 3, it detects a single pink 'person' mask in the upper-left distance (~12–15 m ahead along the sidewalk), merging or missing one of the two closely spaced pedestrians (~0.5 m apart, neither facing nor looking at the camera wearer) who are partially occluded by overhanging foliage. In frame 4, it labels the dark rounded object at the bottom-right foreground (~0.1–0.2 m away, within immediate contact of the camera wearer's head) as a pink 'person' mask as the wearer turns right toward the road. Compared to the RGB image, the segmentation map highlights the presence of the small, distant pedestrian figure in frame 3 against the busy background foliage and trees. However, it is highly unreliable across the sequence: it completely misses the foreground cap/wearer in frames 1, 2, 3, and 5, merges the two distant pedestrians in frame 3 into a single fragmented blob, and provides no spatial masks for any surrounding obstacles within arm's reach.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely blank (pure black) across all five frames, providing no skeletal keypoints for the camera wearer or the distant pedestrians. From the RGB context, the camera wearer's hands and body remain entirely out of the field of view below the camera (apart from the top edge of a dark cap or helmet rim at ~0.1–0.2 m at the bottom of the frame), while the two pedestrians appearing in the upper-left of frame 3 are roughly 12–15 m away along the sidewalk and about 0.5 m apart. In the RGB strip, those two distant people appear to stand side by side facing away or obliquely down the path rather than looking toward the camera wearer, while the camera wearer turns roughly 90 degrees to the right from frames 1 to 5 toward the wet street where a thin curb tree stands within arm's reach (~0.8–1.2 m away on the right). Because the pose map detects nothing, it contributes no spatial information beyond what is visible in the RGB frames and cannot confirm body orientation, gaze direction, or hand reach. The map is unreliable for the distant pair of pedestrians in frame 3 due to their small scale (~12–15 m distance) and partial occlusion by tree branches and foliage.
